subject: Enterprise migration — this was supposed to be done
snippet: Maya, I'll be direct because I think that's fair at this point. The enterprise migration was supposed to be complete by June 30. It's now July 14 and I still don't have a working t
body_text:
Maya,

I'll be direct because I think that's fair at this point. The enterprise migration was supposed to be complete by June 30. It's now July 14 and I still don't have a working timeline from your team — just 'soon' from Dev when I ask.

My CTO is asking me why we're paying for a platform we can't fully cut over to, and I don't have a good answer. I need three things from you directly: what actually happened, a real date I can hold your team to, and some way of knowing you'll hit it this time.

I like Kettle. I've said so internally more than once. But I can't keep covering for a vendor relationship that isn't delivering. Can we talk today?

Dana

meta.action_summary: Dana needs a real root cause, a firm new migration date, and a way to trust it this time.

subject: Re: Enterprise migration — this was supposed to be done
snippet: Dana, You're right to be direct, and I'd rather you were than not. I'm sorry — both for missing June 30 and for the fact that you had to chase Dev for a straight answer instead of
body_text:
Dana,

You're right to be direct, and I'd rather you were than not. I'm sorry — both for missing June 30 and for the fact that you had to chase Dev for a straight answer instead of getting one from me.

Here's what actually happened. Your ledger schema uses a compound key structure for multi-entity transactions that our migration tooling wasn't built to handle — we discovered this three weeks into the cutover, not before, because our test dataset didn't include a multi-entity account like yours. That's on us. We should have caught it in scoping, and Priya's team is redoing our onboarding checklist so the next enterprise migration doesn't get surprised the same way.

Where we actually are: the mapping logic is rewritten and passing against a full copy of your July data in staging. What's left is a dry-run cutover rehearsal and a rollback plan we're comfortable with, given how much trust we've already spent here. I'm not going to give you a date I'm not confident in a second time, so here's the one I am confident in: July 31, with the actual cutover happening the weekend of the 25th so we have a week of headroom before I tell you it's done.

To rebuild some of that trust mechanically rather than just asking for it: you'll get a written status update from me — not Dev, not support — every Friday until this is closed out, whether or not there's news. If we slip again, I want you to hear it from me on a Friday, not discover it on your own three weeks later.

I also want to make this right on the commercial side. I'm crediting Lumenpay 100% of August platform fees regardless of how the migration lands. Wendy will get the credit memo to your AP contact this week so it's not just something I said in an email.

I can do a call today — I have 2pm and 4:30pm PT open, or tomorrow morning if today's too tight on your end. I'd rather talk than have this be the last word by email.

I know 'trust me' doesn't mean much right now. I'm hoping the Friday updates and an actual date that holds will mean more than another promise on a page, and I'd rather earn that back slowly and for real than ask you to just take my word for it a second time.

Maya

meta.action_summary: Maya committed to a July 31 migration completion date, weekly Friday status updates, and a full August fee credit for Lumenpay.
meta.commitment_made_by_user: New migration completion date of July 31 (cutover weekend of July 25), weekly written status updates every Friday until closed out, and a full August platform fee credit.

subject: Re: Following up from our call — some numbers
snippet: Raj, Appreciate you being direct — I'll try to match that. On valuation: $55-60M pre is a real conversation, but I think it undersells where we are. We closed June at $2.3M ARR, up
body_text:
Raj,

Appreciate you being direct — I'll try to match that.

On valuation: $55-60M pre is a real conversation, but I think it undersells where we are. We closed June at $2.3M ARR, up from $1.6M at the start of the year, and that's before Lumenpay's enterprise tier is even fully live — which, to be fair, is the thing giving you pause, so let me address it directly instead of talking around it.

The migration slipped because we underestimated a schema mapping problem, not because the product doesn't work at that scale — it's in staging now against their real data, cutover is the weekend of July 25, and I'm not going to pretend that slip didn't happen or that it shouldn't factor into how you're thinking about execution risk. It should, a little. But I don't think it's a $10M problem, especially with Tarrow Health scaling cleanly on the same enterprise features.

Where I'd actually push back is the framing that Series A comps from February are the ceiling — the two companies I know of that raised in that window did so before the current pullback in growth-stage multiples fully corrected, and I don't think a business at our growth rate should be priced off comps that are already stale. I'd want to talk about something closer to $70-75M pre, with the caveat that I'm more anchored to growth rate and net revenue retention than a headline number, so if there's a structure that gets you comfortable with $70M+ pre in exchange for something other than a flat valuation number, I'm open to that conversation.

On the observer seat — I don't think it's presumptuous, and honestly I'd rather have that conversation now than have it feel like a late add during diligence. My only real ask is that it's contingent on you leading, not a standing offer regardless of outcome. I think that's fair to both of us.

I'd like Ellen and Greg on the next call — partly because they'll have useful context on our board dynamics, and partly because I want you hearing the same numbers from more than just me. I'll have them loop you in with the June board numbers by end of week so you can look at the real detail before we're back on the phone.

Let's find time next week. Thursday works well on my end if it does on yours.

Maya

meta.action_summary: Maya countered at $70-75M pre-money, made the board observer seat contingent on Foundry Line leading, and committed to sharing June board numbers with Raj via Ellen and Greg.

Official kickoff: SOC2 Type II fieldwork starts the week of August 17 with Anchor Assurance LLP, covering the observation period from February 1 through July 31. This is the real one — the Type I we did in the spring was a point-in-time check; this one watches whether we actually followed our own controls for six months straight.

Questions to me or Priya.

subject: State of Kettle — heading into the board meeting
snippet: Team — It's almost 10pm and I've been staring at the board deck outline Sana put together, and I keep thinking you all deserve to hear where things actually stand from me directly
body_text:
Team —

It's almost 10pm and I've been staring at the board deck outline Sana put together, and I keep thinking you all deserve to hear where things actually stand from me directly instead of secondhand or in Friday standup. So — long email, sorry, make coffee.

The headline: June closed at $2.3M ARR, up from $1.6M in January. That's real growth, and it's growth built on two things — Tarrow Health scaling cleanly on the enterprise tier, and, more complicated, Lumenpay.

I want to be straight about Lumenpay because most of you have heard pieces of this but maybe not the whole thing. We missed the June 30 migration date. That's on us collectively, but honestly mostly on me for not pressure-testing the original estimate harder before I gave Dana a date. Dev's team found and fixed the actual problem — a schema mapping issue with how Lumenpay structures multi-entity transactions — and we're now targeting July 31, with cutover the weekend of the 25th. I told Dana that directly and I meant it. If anyone touching that migration sees us at risk of missing it again, I want to know immediately, not after the fact.

On the fundraising side: Foundry Line is real. Raj has proposed terms in the $55-60M pre-money range; I've countered closer to $70-75M based on our growth rate, and we're still talking. Nothing is signed, nothing is close to signed, and I'd ask everyone to keep this one quiet outside this group for now — the last thing we need is speculation making its way to customers or candidates before there's anything real to say.

Hiring: we're down to two strong finalists for Head of Marketing after passing on Priyanka Chatterjee — good candidate, wrong specific gap for where we are. I want someone hands-on with PLG motion, not someone who's managed a team that did it. Sana and Tom are running the final rounds this week.

SOC2 Type II fieldwork starts August 17 — Priya sent details separately, but the short version is this is the real audit, not the point-in-time check from spring, and it matters for both Lumenpay's security team and for Series B diligence, so please don't let evidence collection slip.

AWS: the spend spike from June is mostly explained and mostly fixed — Dev's team found some over-provisioned staging environments that were quietly costing us about $2,600/month more than they should have. Wendy's got the reserved instance purchase approved, which should bring us back toward our normal run rate.

None of this is a crisis. It's just a lot moving at once, which is honestly the normal condition of a Series A company twelve months in, not a special one. I'd rather you hear the real version from me — good and complicated — than a polished one. I'll share the finalized board deck with all of you before it goes out to Ellen, Greg, and Raj, the same as always.

Thanks for how hard everyone's been working on all of this at once. It shows.

M

snippet: Ellen, Greg — Getting you the rough numbers early like we discussed, ahead of the full deck on the 20th. Attached is a summary; headline figures below so you have something to skim
body_text:
Ellen, Greg —

Getting you the rough numbers early like we discussed, ahead of the full deck on the 20th. Attached is a summary; headline figures below so you have something to skim before you open it.

ARR closed June at $2.3M, up from $1.6M at the start of the year — about 44% growth year to date. Net revenue retention is 118%, driven mostly by Tarrow Health's expansion into the enterprise tier in Q2. Gross margin held at 78%.

Runway: 14 months at current burn, assuming we hold hiring to the two open backend engineering reqs through year end and nothing else. That number doesn't assume anything from the Foundry Line conversation — I'd rather board plan against the business we have than a term sheet we don't.

Headcount is 28 today, would be 30 if both open reqs close by September, which is the plan.

The one thing I want to flag before you see it in the deck rather than have it be a surprise: the Lumenpay enterprise migration missed its original June 30 date. New date is July 31, cutover weekend of the 25th. I'll have a clean update on whether that held by the time the full deck goes out on the 20th. I take responsibility for that slip — the original estimate was too optimistic and I should have pressure-tested it harder before committing to Dana.

AWS costs spiked in June (about $2,600/month above normal from some over-provisioned staging environments) — mostly resolved now, reserved instances purchased to lock in the savings going forward.

SOC2 Type II fieldwork starts August 17, which matters for both Lumenpay's security review and eventual Series B diligence.

Let me know if you want to get ahead of any of this on a call before the 20th rather than waiting for the full deck. Happy to walk through the attached in more detail.

Maya

body_text:
Beth —

Given where things already are with Dana, I don't want to pick a fight over language right now unless it's actually dangerous. Broadening to 'any data handling issue' feels too open-ended to just accept, though — can we counter with something scoped to issues arising from our systems or personnel, which still gives them real protection without us signing up for liability over things entirely outside our control?

On referencing the SOC2 report directly in the contract: I'd rather not commit to that yet since the audit isn't done. Let's leave it as 'available upon request following completion' instead of naming a specific report or date we might not hit.

I'll have Dev confirm the SOC2 report language makes sense technically by Friday, then it's yours to send back to their side.

Maya
